decisions.reason: This cutting and creasing finisher fits the firm's core postpress know-how and modular portfolio, so even with limited public market evidence the firm is likely to retain it and learn through service-led customer feedback.

As a homepage-highlighted flagship in print enhancement that supports the firm's move toward automated, higher-value finishing, this product is strongly aligned with existing capabilities and unlikely to be withdrawn soon.

A sheet preparation module is closely related to the firm's established finishing workflow expertise and works as a complement to broader systems, which favors keeping it despite modest visible traction.
This B2-format multifinisher was presented as a strategic focus product and sits squarely in the firm's automation-oriented postpress competence base, making continuation highly likely.

A hybrid saddle stitcher directly serves the firm's booklet-making customer base and builds on service, training, and application knowledge the firm already possesses, so management would probably keep it.
The folding add-on unit already shows evidence of customer deployment and strengthens the firm's modular inline finishing offer, which lowers the chance of near-term withdrawal.
